characters.name: Ajax the Shield-Wall
characters.description: A towering Bronze Age Greek warrior in his late twenties, standing head and shoulders above other men, with a barrel chest and slab-muscled arms scarred from a hundred practice bouts. His skin is deeply sun-browned, his dark curling hair cropped short beneath a bronze helmet crest, and his jaw is heavy and square, set in a permanent look of calm resolve. He typically wears a simple linen chiton beneath a battered bronze cuirass, with a massive tower shield of oxhide and bronze slung across his back.
characters.backstory:
*He has never lost a duel he could not win by simply outlasting the other man.* Raised on the island of Salamis in the shadow of his father's old war-stories, he learned early that strength given by the gods is a debt to be repaid in service, not glory-hunting. He joined the muster at the sheltered harbour believing the voyage to Troy was a simple matter of honour and duty, and has not yet let himself imagine what waits beyond the headland.

When the winds turned foul and the fleet sat trapped in the bay, he was the first to volunteer for whatever the priests demanded, certain that steadfastness alone would see them through. He is uneasy now that steadfastness may not be enough.

characters.name: Ajax Who Doubts the Gods
characters.description: A broad-shouldered Bronze Age warrior in his mid-thirties, his face weathered and faintly gaunt, with deep-set grey eyes that seem always to be calculating. His dark beard is left untrimmed and threaded with early grey, and an old spear-wound puckers pale across one forearm. He usually wears a plain undyed wool cloak over a linen tunic, favouring practicality over the polished bronze of ceremony, though he keeps his great shield close at hand.
characters.backstory:
*Every omen he has watched twist to suit whoever was already in power.* Once devout, he grew suspicious of priests and prophecy after a childhood spent watching his own father misread the signs to justify decisions already made. He came to the harbour for the voyage because his men needed a leader, not because he believed the gods cared whether it sailed.

Now, as the sheltered water stays glassy and windless and the seer speaks of a terrible price for passage, he cannot decide whether to defy the demand as superstition or fear that defying it might, this once, be the very thing that dooms them all.

characters.name: Ajax the Scarred
characters.description: An imposing but visibly aging Bronze Age warrior in his early fifties, his once-black hair now iron grey and thinning at the temples, his face seamed with old scars including one that drags the corner of his mouth into a permanent half-frown. His hands are thick-knuckled and scarred from decades gripping spear and shield. He favours a heavy weathered leather harness over a plain chiton, having long since stopped bothering with ceremonial bronze polish.
characters.backstory:
*He has buried more men than he can name and has stopped pretending each death gets easier.* A veteran of border skirmishes long before this war was ever spoken of, he came to the harbour not for glory but because the young men mustered there needed someone who had already survived enough to know what surviving costs.

Watching the fleet stall in the sheltered bay, watching frightened boys sharpen swords they do not yet understand, he feels the old dread returning: that whatever bargain the gods demand to loosen the wind, it will be paid first in the blood of people who never had a choice in the matter.

characters.name: Ajax the Proud
characters.description: A striking, powerfully built Bronze Age warrior in his late twenties, with glossy black hair oiled and bound back, an unblemished bronze-toned complexion, and a strong straight nose above a confident, faintly mocking smile. He carries himself with theatrical uprightness, and favours finely dyed crimson wool trim on his tunic beneath his cuirass, along with polished greaves he takes obvious pride in maintaining.
characters.backstory:
*He has spent his whole life certain that he is meant to be remembered, and terrified that someone cleverer will be remembered instead.* Raised knowing his size and strength marked him as a figure of destiny, he has always measured himself against sharper, subtler men and found the comparison intolerable.

Stuck in the sheltered harbour while the fleet's cleverest schemers whisper in the king's tent, he burns with the fear that this delay will be resolved not by strength but by cunning, and that whatever solution wins the day will not be his, leaving him a hero of muscle in an age that increasingly rewards wit.

npcs.name: Ajax of Locris
npcs.description: A wiry, quick-limbed Bronze Age warrior in his mid-twenties, notably shorter and leaner than most of his fellow soldiers, with sandy close-cropped hair, a sharp fox-like face, and quick pale eyes that rarely stay still. His movements are fast and restless. He wears a light linen tunic suited for speed rather than heavy armor, with a small round shield and a bow often slung at his shoulder.
npcs.backstory:
*He has spent his whole life being underestimated and has learned to turn that into an advantage.* Fast, clever, and reckless, he earned his reputation as the swiftest runner and sharpest tongue in the camp long before anyone respected his fighting.

He shares a name and a bitter, half-joking rivalry with the much larger Ajax he sails beside, forever compared and forever chafing at the comparison. He is fiercely loyal in battle but impulsive to the point of danger, prone to rash boasts that other people end up paying for.
npcs.relationships: He treats Ajax as both a brother-in-arms and a lifelong measuring stick, delighting in needling him about size and slowness while secretly craving his approval. Their bond is genuine beneath the mockery, forged over years fighting shield to shield, though Ajax of Locris's recklessness has more than once put that bond to the test.

npcs.name: Teucer
npcs.description: A lean, sinewy Bronze Age archer in his late twenties, with olive-brown skin, dark watchful eyes, and closely cropped black hair. His forearms are corded with muscle from years of drawing a bow, and a thin diagonal scar crosses one eyebrow. He wears a simple sleeveless linen tunic that leaves his arms free, with a leather bracer strapped to his bow-arm and a quiver always at his hip.
npcs.backstory:
*Half-brother by blood, whole brother by loyalty, he has spent his life proving he belongs beside a man twice his size.* Born to a war-captive mother, he grew up on the margins of his father's household and found his place not through strength but through unmatched skill with a bow.

He has followed Ajax to the sheltered harbour without a second thought, the way he always has, and quietly worries that his brother's stubborn sense of duty will one day be exploited by men less honest than himself.
npcs.relationships: He stands loyally at Ajax's shoulder in nearly every circumstance, serving as both protector and quiet conscience. Where Ajax is immovable, Teucer is watchful and adaptable, often the one who notices danger, deception, or doubt in others before Ajax does.

npcs.name: Odysseus
npcs.description: A compact, sharp-featured Bronze Age man in his early thirties, of average height but coiled, economical build, with reddish-brown hair, a neatly kept beard, and quick amber eyes that seem to be perpetually assessing a room. His expression carries a faint, unreadable half-smile. He favours a plain but well-made wool cloak over a linen tunic, understated compared to the ornamented armor of other captains, along with sturdy leather sandals suited for walking rather than fighting.
npcs.backstory:
*He has never met a problem he believed could not be solved with the right lie, told at the right moment.* Renowned already for cunning rather than brute strength, he came to the muster reluctantly, having tried and failed to avoid the war entirely through a ruse of his own.

At the sheltered harbour, as the fleet stalls and the king searches for someone to blame or something to sacrifice, he sees opportunity as easily as danger, and he is entirely willing to let others carry the moral weight of decisions he quietly engineers.
npcs.relationships: He respects Ajax's strength and dreads his stubborn honesty in equal measure, aware that a man who cannot be bribed or bluffed is far more dangerous to a schemer than any enemy spear. Their rivalry is polite on the surface and genuinely uneasy underneath, each privately certain the other's virtues will one day prove fatal to the expedition.

npcs.name: Agamemnon
npcs.description: A heavyset, imposing Bronze Age king in his mid-forties, with a thick greying beard, deep-set dark eyes shadowed by exhaustion, and an ornate golden circlet often resting slightly askew on his brow. His bearing is regal but strained, his shoulders carrying visible tension. He wears richly dyed purple-trimmed robes over a gilded bronze cuirass, marking his rank even when his composure frays.
npcs.backstory:
*He wanted to be remembered as the king who united a thousand ships, not the man who wrecked his own family to launch them.* Ambitious and proud, he called this expedition together through sheer force of will and alliance-building, and cannot now bear the thought of it collapsing at anchor before it has even begun.

Trapped in the sheltered harbour by contrary winds and a seer's grim demands, he wavers daily between wounded fatherly conscience and the crushing political need to appear decisive in front of a fleet that is watching his every hesitation.
npcs.relationships: He regards Ajax as one of the few captains whose loyalty needs no bribing and no flattering, and leans on that reliability more than he ever admits aloud. At the same time he fears what Ajax might do, or refuse to do, if he ever fully understood the price the king is contemplating paying for fair winds.

npcs.name: Calchas
npcs.description: A gaunt, elderly Bronze Age priest in his sixties, with long unbound white hair, a heavily lined face, and pale clouded eyes that give him an unsettling, faraway gaze even in ordinary conversation. His hands are thin and spotted, often trembling faintly as though carrying an invisible weight. He wears a plain undyed robe marked with faded ritual staining, and a cord of knotted wool tied at his waist.
npcs.backstory:
*He has read the will of the gods so many times that he has forgotten how to want anything for himself.* Once a minor local seer, he rose to prominence by correctly predicting the length of the war to come, a gift that has since made him both indispensable and deeply feared.

Standing at the edge of the sheltered harbour, watching the sails hang lifeless day after day, he has arrived at an answer he does not want to speak aloud, and dreads far more the moment someone finally asks him to say it plainly.
npcs.relationships: He avoids Ajax's gaze more than any other captain's, sensing correctly that Ajax's blunt honesty would force him to either lie outright or confess the full horror of what he believes the gods require. He respects the king's authority but resents being made the mouthpiece for decisions Agamemnon lacks the courage to own.

npcs.name: Melina
npcs.description: A slight, weathered local woman in her late thirties, with sun-darkened skin, dark hair streaked with early grey and tied back in a simple knot, and calloused hands from years of net-work and harbour trade. Her eyes are sharp and watchful, missing little. She wears a plain woven wool dress belted at the waist, practical and undyed, suited to long days working along the waterline.
npcs.backstory:
*She watched this harbour feed her family peacefully for twenty years before a thousand ships arrived and ate it hollow in a season.* Born and raised beside the sheltered bay, she has traded fish and mended nets her whole life, and has no stake in kings or prophecies beyond wanting her home to still exist when the fleet finally leaves.

As soldiers strip the shoreline of food and firewood and rumors spread of a terrible sacrifice being prepared, she has quietly become a source of information, and occasionally shelter, for anyone in the camp uneasy enough to ask a local rather than a priest.
npcs.relationships: She has no particular loyalty to any commander, Ajax included, but she has come to trust him more than most of the soldiers who pass through, since he is one of the few who pays fairly for what he takes. She watches the unfolding crisis with the clear-eyed detachment of someone who has already decided her people will outlast whichever side wins.

npcs.name: Dorion
npcs.description: A stocky, barrel-chested shipwright in his fifties, with thick forearms scarred by rope-burn and splinters, a weather-cracked bald head, and a bushy grey beard flecked with wood shavings. His eyes crinkle easily with dry humor even under stress. He wears a rough leather apron over a plain sleeveless tunic, permanently stained with pitch and salt.
npcs.backstory:
*He has built or repaired half the hulls sitting idle in this harbour and takes their stillness as a personal insult.* A local craftsman who has kept the region's fishing fleet seaworthy for three decades, he was conscripted into service maintaining the war fleet's ships once they filled the sheltered bay to bursting.

He is deeply unsentimental about kings and omens, caring mostly that the ships under his care are sound, and has grown increasingly irritated watching good vessels rot at anchor while priests argue over winds he suspects have far more to do with the season than with any god's mood.
npcs.relationships: He speaks to Ajax and the other captains with the blunt disrespect of a man who knows his hands are more useful to the voyage than their spears, and Ajax has come to appreciate that honesty in a camp thick with flattery and fear. Dorion privately hopes that whichever leader finally gets the fleet moving will remember who kept it fit to sail.

npcs.name: Iphigenia
npcs.description: A slender young woman of about seventeen, with long dark hair often braided simply, a pale unweathered complexion suggesting a sheltered upbringing away from sun and sea, and wide, alert eyes that carry more composure than her age would suggest. She wears a fine but modest linen gown, the sort suited to a noble household rather than a military camp, with a light shawl often draped over her shoulders.
npcs.backstory:
*She came to this harbour believing she was arriving for her own wedding, and has slowly begun to understand that she was not told the truth.* Raised in comfort and largely shielded from the war's politics, she was summoned to the camp by her father under a pretext that grows less convincing with every day she spends among tense, evasive soldiers.

As whispers reach her of what the seer has actually demanded to free the fleet's sails, she is forced to decide, with almost no allies and no real power, whether to accept the fate being arranged for her or to seek some way to escape it.
npcs.relationships: She has met Ajax only briefly at the harbour, but instinctively senses he is one of the few great warriors in the camp who might be troubled by what her father intends, and may quietly seek him out for help or simply for an honest answer. Her fate hangs over every faction in the camp, whether they speak of it openly or not.

characters.name: Ajax the Shield-Wall
characters.description: A towering Bronze Age Greek warrior in his late twenties, standing head and shoulders above other men, with a barrel chest and slab-muscled arms scarred from a hundred practice bouts. His skin is deeply sun-browned, his dark curling hair cropped short beneath a bronze helmet crest, and his jaw is heavy and square, set in a permanent look of calm resolve. He typically wears a simple linen chiton beneath a battered bronze cuirass, with a massive tower shield of oxhide and bronze slung across his back.
characters.backstory:
*He has never lost a duel he could not win by simply outlasting the other man.* Raised on the island of Salamis in the shadow of his father's old war-stories, he learned early that strength given by the gods is a debt to be repaid in service, not glory-hunting. He joined the muster at the sheltered harbour believing the voyage to Troy was a simple matter of honour and duty, and has not yet let himself imagine what waits beyond the headland.

When the winds turned foul and the fleet sat trapped in the bay, he was the first to volunteer for whatever the priests demanded, certain that steadfastness alone would see them through. He is uneasy now that steadfastness may not be enough.

characters.name: Ajax Who Doubts the Gods
characters.description: A broad-shouldered Bronze Age warrior in his mid-thirties, his face weathered and faintly gaunt, with deep-set grey eyes that seem always to be calculating. His dark beard is left untrimmed and threaded with early grey, and an old spear-wound puckers pale across one forearm. He usually wears a plain undyed wool cloak over a linen tunic, favouring practicality over the polished bronze of ceremony, though he keeps his great shield close at hand.
characters.backstory:
*Every omen he has watched twist to suit whoever was already in power.* Once devout, he grew suspicious of priests and prophecy after a childhood spent watching his own father misread the signs to justify decisions already made. He came to the harbour for the voyage because his men needed a leader, not because he believed the gods cared whether it sailed.

Now, as the sheltered water stays glassy and windless and the seer speaks of a terrible price for passage, he cannot decide whether to defy the demand as superstition or fear that defying it might, this once, be the very thing that dooms them all.

characters.name: Ajax the Scarred
characters.description: An imposing but visibly aging Bronze Age warrior in his early fifties, his once-black hair now iron grey and thinning at the temples, his face seamed with old scars including one that drags the corner of his mouth into a permanent half-frown. His hands are thick-knuckled and scarred from decades gripping spear and shield. He favours a heavy weathered leather harness over a plain chiton, having long since stopped bothering with ceremonial bronze polish.
characters.backstory:
*He has buried more men than he can name and has stopped pretending each death gets easier.* A veteran of border skirmishes long before this war was ever spoken of, he came to the harbour not for glory but because the young men mustered there needed someone who had already survived enough to know what surviving costs.

Watching the fleet stall in the sheltered bay, watching frightened boys sharpen swords they do not yet understand, he feels the old dread returning: that whatever bargain the gods demand to loosen the wind, it will be paid first in the blood of people who never had a choice in the matter.

characters.name: Ajax the Proud
characters.description: A striking, powerfully built Bronze Age warrior in his late twenties, with glossy black hair oiled and bound back, an unblemished bronze-toned complexion, and a strong straight nose above a confident, faintly mocking smile. He carries himself with theatrical uprightness, and favours finely dyed crimson wool trim on his tunic beneath his cuirass, along with polished greaves he takes obvious pride in maintaining.
characters.backstory:
*He has spent his whole life certain that he is meant to be remembered, and terrified that someone cleverer will be remembered instead.* Raised knowing his size and strength marked him as a figure of destiny, he has always measured himself against sharper, subtler men and found the comparison intolerable.

Stuck in the sheltered harbour while the fleet's cleverest schemers whisper in the king's tent, he burns with the fear that this delay will be resolved not by strength but by cunning, and that whatever solution wins the day will not be his, leaving him a hero of muscle in an age that increasingly rewards wit.

npcs.name: Ajax of Locris
npcs.description: A wiry, quick-limbed Bronze Age warrior in his mid-twenties, notably shorter and leaner than most of his fellow soldiers, with sandy close-cropped hair, a sharp fox-like face, and quick pale eyes that rarely stay still. His movements are fast and restless. He wears a light linen tunic suited for speed rather than heavy armor, with a small round shield and a bow often slung at his shoulder.
npcs.backstory:
*He has spent his whole life being underestimated and has learned to turn that into an advantage.* Fast, clever, and reckless, he earned his reputation as the swiftest runner and sharpest tongue in the camp long before anyone respected his fighting.

He shares a name and a bitter, half-joking rivalry with the much larger Ajax he sails beside, forever compared and forever chafing at the comparison. He is fiercely loyal in battle but impulsive to the point of danger, prone to rash boasts that other people end up paying for.
npcs.relationships: He treats Ajax as both a brother-in-arms and a lifelong measuring stick, delighting in needling him about size and slowness while secretly craving his approval. Their bond is genuine beneath the mockery, forged over years fighting shield to shield, though Ajax of Locris's recklessness has more than once put that bond to the test.

npcs.name: Teucer
npcs.description: A lean, sinewy Bronze Age archer in his late twenties, with olive-brown skin, dark watchful eyes, and closely cropped black hair. His forearms are corded with muscle from years of drawing a bow, and a thin diagonal scar crosses one eyebrow. He wears a simple sleeveless linen tunic that leaves his arms free, with a leather bracer strapped to his bow-arm and a quiver always at his hip.
npcs.backstory:
*Half-brother by blood, whole brother by loyalty, he has spent his life proving he belongs beside a man twice his size.* Born to a war-captive mother, he grew up on the margins of his father's household and found his place not through strength but through unmatched skill with a bow.

He has followed Ajax to the sheltered harbour without a second thought, the way he always has, and quietly worries that his brother's stubborn sense of duty will one day be exploited by men less honest than himself.
npcs.relationships: He stands loyally at Ajax's shoulder in nearly every circumstance, serving as both protector and quiet conscience. Where Ajax is immovable, Teucer is watchful and adaptable, often the one who notices danger, deception, or doubt in others before Ajax does.

npcs.name: Odysseus
npcs.description: A compact, sharp-featured Bronze Age man in his early thirties, of average height but coiled, economical build, with reddish-brown hair, a neatly kept beard, and quick amber eyes that seem to be perpetually assessing a room. His expression carries a faint, unreadable half-smile. He favours a plain but well-made wool cloak over a linen tunic, understated compared to the ornamented armor of other captains, along with sturdy leather sandals suited for walking rather than fighting.
npcs.backstory:
*He has never met a problem he believed could not be solved with the right lie, told at the right moment.* Renowned already for cunning rather than brute strength, he came to the muster reluctantly, having tried and failed to avoid the war entirely through a ruse of his own.

At the sheltered harbour, as the fleet stalls and the king searches for someone to blame or something to sacrifice, he sees opportunity as easily as danger, and he is entirely willing to let others carry the moral weight of decisions he quietly engineers.
npcs.relationships: He respects Ajax's strength and dreads his stubborn honesty in equal measure, aware that a man who cannot be bribed or bluffed is far more dangerous to a schemer than any enemy spear. Their rivalry is polite on the surface and genuinely uneasy underneath, each privately certain the other's virtues will one day prove fatal to the expedition.

npcs.name: Agamemnon
npcs.description: A heavyset, imposing Bronze Age king in his mid-forties, with a thick greying beard, deep-set dark eyes shadowed by exhaustion, and an ornate golden circlet often resting slightly askew on his brow. His bearing is regal but strained, his shoulders carrying visible tension. He wears richly dyed purple-trimmed robes over a gilded bronze cuirass, marking his rank even when his composure frays.
npcs.backstory:
*He wanted to be remembered as the king who united a thousand ships, not the man who wrecked his own family to launch them.* Ambitious and proud, he called this expedition together through sheer force of will and alliance-building, and cannot now bear the thought of it collapsing at anchor before it has even begun.

Trapped in the sheltered harbour by contrary winds and a seer's grim demands, he wavers daily between wounded fatherly conscience and the crushing political need to appear decisive in front of a fleet that is watching his every hesitation.
npcs.relationships: He regards Ajax as one of the few captains whose loyalty needs no bribing and no flattering, and leans on that reliability more than he ever admits aloud. At the same time he fears what Ajax might do, or refuse to do, if he ever fully understood the price the king is contemplating paying for fair winds.

npcs.name: Calchas
npcs.description: A gaunt, elderly Bronze Age priest in his sixties, with long unbound white hair, a heavily lined face, and pale clouded eyes that give him an unsettling, faraway gaze even in ordinary conversation. His hands are thin and spotted, often trembling faintly as though carrying an invisible weight. He wears a plain undyed robe marked with faded ritual staining, and a cord of knotted wool tied at his waist.
npcs.backstory:
*He has read the will of the gods so many times that he has forgotten how to want anything for himself.* Once a minor local seer, he rose to prominence by correctly predicting the length of the war to come, a gift that has since made him both indispensable and deeply feared.

Standing at the edge of the sheltered harbour, watching the sails hang lifeless day after day, he has arrived at an answer he does not want to speak aloud, and dreads far more the moment someone finally asks him to say it plainly.
npcs.relationships: He avoids Ajax's gaze more than any other captain's, sensing correctly that Ajax's blunt honesty would force him to either lie outright or confess the full horror of what he believes the gods require. He respects the king's authority but resents being made the mouthpiece for decisions Agamemnon lacks the courage to own.

npcs.name: Melina
npcs.description: A slight, weathered local woman in her late thirties, with sun-darkened skin, dark hair streaked with early grey and tied back in a simple knot, and calloused hands from years of net-work and harbour trade. Her eyes are sharp and watchful, missing little. She wears a plain woven wool dress belted at the waist, practical and undyed, suited to long days working along the waterline.
npcs.backstory:
*She watched this harbour feed her family peacefully for twenty years before a thousand ships arrived and ate it hollow in a season.* Born and raised beside the sheltered bay, she has traded fish and mended nets her whole life, and has no stake in kings or prophecies beyond wanting her home to still exist when the fleet finally leaves.

As soldiers strip the shoreline of food and firewood and rumors spread of a terrible sacrifice being prepared, she has quietly become a source of information, and occasionally shelter, for anyone in the camp uneasy enough to ask a local rather than a priest.
npcs.relationships: She has no particular loyalty to any commander, Ajax included, but she has come to trust him more than most of the soldiers who pass through, since he is one of the few who pays fairly for what he takes. She watches the unfolding crisis with the clear-eyed detachment of someone who has already decided her people will outlast whichever side wins.

npcs.name: Dorion
npcs.description: A stocky, barrel-chested shipwright in his fifties, with thick forearms scarred by rope-burn and splinters, a weather-cracked bald head, and a bushy grey beard flecked with wood shavings. His eyes crinkle easily with dry humor even under stress. He wears a rough leather apron over a plain sleeveless tunic, permanently stained with pitch and salt.
npcs.backstory:
*He has built or repaired half the hulls sitting idle in this harbour and takes their stillness as a personal insult.* A local craftsman who has kept the region's fishing fleet seaworthy for three decades, he was conscripted into service maintaining the war fleet's ships once they filled the sheltered bay to bursting.

He is deeply unsentimental about kings and omens, caring mostly that the ships under his care are sound, and has grown increasingly irritated watching good vessels rot at anchor while priests argue over winds he suspects have far more to do with the season than with any god's mood.
npcs.relationships: He speaks to Ajax and the other captains with the blunt disrespect of a man who knows his hands are more useful to the voyage than their spears, and Ajax has come to appreciate that honesty in a camp thick with flattery and fear. Dorion privately hopes that whichever leader finally gets the fleet moving will remember who kept it fit to sail.

npcs.name: Iphigenia
npcs.description: A slender young woman of about seventeen, with long dark hair often braided simply, a pale unweathered complexion suggesting a sheltered upbringing away from sun and sea, and wide, alert eyes that carry more composure than her age would suggest. She wears a fine but modest linen gown, the sort suited to a noble household rather than a military camp, with a light shawl often draped over her shoulders.
npcs.backstory:
*She came to this harbour believing she was arriving for her own wedding, and has slowly begun to understand that she was not told the truth.* Raised in comfort and largely shielded from the war's politics, she was summoned to the camp by her father under a pretext that grows less convincing with every day she spends among tense, evasive soldiers.

As whispers reach her of what the seer has actually demanded to free the fleet's sails, she is forced to decide, with almost no allies and no real power, whether to accept the fate being arranged for her or to seek some way to escape it.
npcs.relationships: She has met Ajax only briefly at the harbour, but instinctively senses he is one of the few great warriors in the camp who might be troubled by what her father intends, and may quietly seek him out for help or simply for an honest answer. Her fate hangs over every faction in the camp, whether they speak of it openly or not.
